scenes.name: Kids & pets
scenes.blurb: A child running across the garden.

why.shutter: Fast enough to stop a running child dead.
why.aperture: A touch off wide open. At 1/1000 in daylight you still have light to spare, and it buys you a margin on focus you will be glad of.
why.focal: Close enough to fill the frame without standing on top of them.

why.focal: The long end, so the background is magnified and the face is not stretched.

scenes.name: Panning
scenes.blurb: Following something past you, so it stays sharp and the world does not.

why.shutter: Slow, on purpose. You turn with the subject and the background smears.
why.aperture: Right down, and not for depth: a thirtieth of a second in daylight is far more light than the lowest ISO can take.
why.focal: Enough reach to stand safely off the road.

lens.verdict: Your 50 mm will not do this: it is 50 mm at its longest, and this wants 105 mm.
lines: You can walk closer instead, but the subject then sits against a background that has grown behind it, which is a different photograph.
The standard 24 to 105 mm zoom does reach 105 mm, so put that on.

lens.verdict: Your 50 mm f/1.8 does this, and does it better than the standard zoom.
lines: Wide open at f/1.8 it is 2.3 stops brighter than the f/4 on the card, so the camera drops the ISO by the same amount.
The background will also go softer than the photograph above, which is what people mean when they say a fast lens looks different.
